content.intro: Print a dominoes score sheet for block or draw dominoes, or keep score on your phone. Play to 100, 150 or 250, and the sheet shows the winner as soon as someone gets there.
howToUse: Write each player's name at the top of a column; with four players in partnerships, give each team a column. Only one player scores each hand, so write the points in that player's column and leave the others empty.

When a player goes out, add up the pips on every tile left in the other players' hands and write the total for the winner. If the hand blocks and nobody can play, the player with the fewest pips scores the pips in the other hands.
The first player to reach the target wins: 100 is the usual game, with 150 or 250 for a longer one. Choose the target under Play to on the online sheet; it adds every hand and announces the winner.

howToPlay.heading: How a hand of dominoes works
paragraphs: A standard double-6 set has 28 tiles. With two to four players, each draws seven tiles and the rest stay face down as the boneyard. The first tile is set down in the middle, often the highest double, and the line of play grows from both ends: every tile must match the number on the open end it joins.

In draw dominoes, a player who cannot match either end draws from the boneyard until they can play or the boneyard is empty. In block dominoes there is no drawing: a player who cannot play simply passes. Draw games run longer and suit two players; block games are quicker and are common with four.

The hand ends when someone plays their last tile, often called dominoing, or when it blocks because nobody can play. The pips left in the losers' hands go to the winner, and new hands are dealt until someone reaches the target.

tips: Count both halves of every tile. A 6-5 is 11 points, and the double-blank is 0.
Many tables round each hand to the nearest 5, so 19 becomes 20. If you play that way, write the rounded number.
In a blocked hand some tables give the winner only the difference between their own pips and the others'. Agree which before the first hand.
With four players in partnerships, count a hand as won by the team, and score the pips left in both opponents' hands.

faqs.a: The player who plays their last tile scores the total pips on the tiles left in every other player's hand. Nobody else scores that hand. The first player to reach the target wins.

faqs.q: How many points do you play to in dominoes?
faqs.a: 100 is the most common target, with 150 or 250 for a longer game. Some groups play to 50 or 200; on paper the sheet works for any target.

faqs.q: What is the difference between block and draw dominoes?
faqs.a: In draw dominoes, a player who cannot play draws tiles from the boneyard. In block dominoes there is no drawing, and a player who cannot play passes.

faqs.q: What happens when a game of dominoes is blocked?
faqs.a: If nobody can play, everyone counts their pips and the player with the lowest count wins the hand and scores the other players' pips. Some tables score only the difference.

faqs.q: How many dominoes does each player get?
faqs.a: With a double-6 set, seven tiles each for two, three or four players. The rest stay in the boneyard.

faqs.q: How many people can play dominoes?
faqs.a: Two to four with a double-6 set, either alone or with four as two partnerships. For bigger groups, Mexican Train or Chicken Foot with a double-9 or double-12 set works better.
